With the exception of monks and nuns, if one instructs others not to relinquish [the offense], whether a formal reprimand is issued or not, it is in all cases a duṣkṛta.
For a bhikṣu, it is a duṣkṛta;
for a śikṣamāṇā, a śrāmaṇera, or a śrāmaṇerī, it is a duṣkṛta.
This is called an offense.

There is no offense if: one renounces [the matter] at the first word; or if the censure is carried out by an illegal separate assembly; or by an illegal united assembly; or by a legal separate assembly; or by a semblance-of-dharma separate assembly; or by a semblance-of-dharma united assembly; or if it is not according to the Dharma, not according to the Vinaya, and not as taught by the Buddha; or if no censure is performed at all. In these cases, there is no offense.
There is no offense in the following cases: when the precept has not yet been established; when one is insane, mentally deranged, or overwhelmed by intense physical pain.
Thus ends the sixteenth [section]. At that time, the Buddha was staying at the Gośīrṣa Garden in Kauśāmbī.
At that time, there was a bhikṣuṇī named Kālī who delighted in quarreling and was unskilled at remembering the matters of dispute; later, she became resentful and spoke these words:
"The Saṃgha has favoritism, anger, fear, and delusion."

When the bhikṣuṇīs heard this, among them were those who had few desires and were contented, who practiced the dhūta austerities, who delighted in training in the precepts, and who possessed a sense of shame and remorse. They reproached the bhikṣuṇī Kālī, saying:
"How can you delight in quarreling and fail to properly remember the matter of the dispute, only later, out of anger, making such a statement as:
'The Saṃgha has favoritism, has hatred, has fear, and has delusion'?"
At that time, the bhikṣuṇīs went and informed the bhikṣus, and the bhikṣus went and informed the World-Honored One.
On that occasion, the World-Honored One, for this reason, assembled the community of bhikṣus and rebuked the bhikṣuṇī Kālī, saying:
"What you have done is wrong; it is not proper conduct, not the Dharma of a śramaṇa, not a pure practice, and not a compliant practice—it is something that should not be done."
"How is it that you take delight in quarreling and do not properly remember the matter of the dispute, yet later, out of anger, speak these words:
'The Saṃgha has favoritism, has ill will, has fear, and has delusion'?"
At that time, after the World-Honored One had rebuked her with countless skillful means, he addressed the bhikṣus:

"From this day forward, I authorize the Saṃgha to perform a formal act of *jñapti-caturtha-karman* (a motion followed by three proclamations) to reprimand the bhikṣuṇī Kālī and cause her to relinquish this matter."
It should be done in this manner.
From among the community of nuns, one who is capable of performing the *karmavācanā* should be appointed as described above, and the following motion (*jñapti*) should be made:
"Sisters of the Sangha, please listen!..."
This Bhikṣuṇī Kālī delighted in quarreling and was unskillful at retaining the matters of dispute; later, out of anger, she spoke these words:
"The Saṃgha has favoritism, has hatred, has fear, and has delusion."
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha now carry out a formal reprimand against the bhikṣuṇī Kālī for this matter: 'Sister!

"The Sangha has attachment, aversion, fear,
and delusion," yet the Sangha is without attachment, without aversion, without fear, and without delusion. Sister!

"The Saṃgha has finished carrying out the formal act of censure against the bhikṣuṇī Kālī for her to abandon this matter. Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter shall be held as such."

From this day forward, I shall establish a precept for the bhikṣuṇīs, encompassing the ten points of meaning and leading to the long endurance of the True Dharma. One who wishes to recite the precepts should do so as follows:
"If a bhikṣuṇī delights in quarreling and is unwilling to properly remember the matters of dispute, and later, out of anger, speaks these words:

and delusion,” yet the Saṅgha is without attachment, without aversion, without fear, and without delusion.
It is you yourself who have attachment, aversion, fear, and delusion.

When that bhikṣuṇī admonishes the other bhikṣuṇī and she persists in her refusal to relinquish [the matter], that bhikṣuṇī should admonish her up to three times so that she may abandon this course of action.
If she abandons it after being admonished up to three times, it is well;
if she does not abandon it, that bhikṣuṇī has committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense involving three rules that must be relinquished.
The meaning of "bhikṣuṇī" is as explained above.

There are four kinds of disputes: disputes concerning speech (*vāda-vivāda*), disputes concerning accusations (*anuvāda-vivāda*), disputes concerning offenses (*āpatti-vivāda*), and disputes concerning legal matters (*adhikaraṇa-vivāda*).
The Sangha consists of a single *kamma* and a single recitation of the *pātimokkha*.

"If she complies with what was said, it is well; if she does not comply, and the three *karmavācanās* have been completed, it is a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*.

if they do not carry out the censure, it is a duṣkṛta.

"Do not abandon it.
If one utters a reprimand, it is a sthūlātyaya;

Except for monks and nuns, if one instructs others not to relinquish [the precepts], it is a *duṣkṛta* offense in all cases.
For a monk, it is a *duṣkṛta*;
for a *śikṣamāṇā*, a *śrāmaṇera*, or a *śrāmaṇerī*, it is a *duṣkṛta*.

This is called an offense. There is no offense if one desists at the first word; or if one is rebuked by an illegal separate assembly; or by an illegal harmonious assembly; or by a legal separate assembly; or by an assembly that resembles the legal but is separate; or by an assembly that resembles the legal but is harmonious; or if it is something that is neither legal nor according to the Vinaya, nor taught by the Buddha; or if one does not perform any rebuke at all. In these cases, there is no offense.
There is no offense in the following cases: when the precept has not yet been established; or when one is insane, mentally deranged, or overwhelmed by intense physical pain.
