"That place is far away, and I could not return on the same day; furthermore, the Buddha has not yet permitted such a journey for this purpose."
They went and informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"From this day forward, when such circumstances arise, I permit you to go away for seven days, whether there be benefit or lack of benefit, provided you return within those seven days."
At that time, there was a minister of faith and devotion who invited the bhikṣu, saying:
"Venerable One, come!
I wish to see you."
The bhikṣu thought to himself:
"That place is far away and I cannot return on the same day; furthermore, the Buddha has not yet permitted going for such a matter.
He went and informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"From this day forward, it is permitted to go away for seven days when such circumstances arise.
This faithful lay follower (upāsaka), whether due to illness, or due to various matters of distress, or for the sake of gain, must return within seven days."
At that time, there were parents who lacked faith and devotion who invited a bhikṣu, saying:
"Venerable sir, come!
We wish to see you."
The bhikṣu thought to himself:
"That place is far away; I cannot return on the same day, yet the Buddha has not yet permitted going for such a matter.
He went and informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:

"From this day forward, when such circumstances arise, I permit you to go away for seven days. If they do not have faith and joy, teach them so that they may have faith and joy; if they observe evil precepts, teach them so that they may uphold the precepts; if they are stingy and greedy, teach them so that they may practice generosity; if they lack wisdom, teach them so that they may possess wisdom—and you must return within seven days."
At that time, there were parents who were faithful and devoted; they sent a messenger to invite the bhikṣu, saying:
"Venerable One, please come!
We wish to see you."
The bhikṣu thought to himself:
"That place is far away and I cannot return on the same day; furthermore, the Buddha has not yet permitted going for such a matter.
He went and informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:

"From this day forward, it is permitted to go away for seven days when such circumstances exist: if one’s parents are faithful and devoted, or if one is ill, or if there are matters of distress and anxiety, or if there are matters of benefit—and to return within seven days."
At that time, a mother invited a bhikṣu, saying:
"Venerable sir, please come; I wish to see you.
The bhikṣu thought to himself:
"It is too far from there to return on the same day; the Buddha has not yet permitted such a matter to go and report to him.
The Buddha said, "From this day forward, if such a matter arises, you are permitted to stay for seven days and must return within those seven days."
At that time, there was a father who invited the bhikṣus in this same manner;
so too did his brothers, sisters, and all his kinsmen and acquaintances.

At that time, there was a bhikṣu who recited sixty kinds of sūtras, such as the *Brahmajāla-sūtra*. Desiring to travel among the people in search of others with whom he might recite together, he set out on his journey.
The bhikṣu thought to himself:
"That place is so far that I cannot return on the same day, yet the Buddha has not yet permitted us to go on such an errand.
He went to inform the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"From this day forward, it is permitted that when such circumstances arise, one may go away for seven days and return within seven days.
At that time, a bhikṣu who had been traveling on a journey had business requiring him to go among the forest trees;
he thought to himself, "That place is distant, and I will not be able to return by the end of the day."
They went to inform the Buddha,
and the Buddha said, "From this day forward, when such circumstances arise, I permit you to go away for seven days and return within those seven days.
At that time, the people of a border state rebelled against King Prasenajit, who personally led his army to suppress them.
The robes, food, drink, and other necessities that the King provided for the Buddha and the Sangha were seized by the ministers who lacked faith and joy, and were not given to them.
The bhikṣus wished to go and inform the King, but they thought to themselves:
"That place is far away; we would not be able to return on the same day, and the Buddha has not yet permitted us to go on such an errand."

That bhikṣu fulfills the earlier rains retreat; having not violated his original commitment, he is without offense.

Whoever enters a village first to beg for alms shall return first to sweep the dining area, spread out the mats, prepare the water vessels, prepare the foot-washing vessels, and prepare the food containers; each person shall then bring their own food and place it in the dining area."
If one obtains a large amount of food, one should first set aside a portion.
If the meal is sufficient, one should eat it; having finished eating, one returns to the dwelling in silence.
If there are others who subsequently enter the village to beg for food, they should return as soon as they have obtained food and bring their alms to the place where the meal is being taken.
If one receives a large amount of food, one should first set aside a portion.
If it is sufficient, one should eat; if it is insufficient, one should take the previously set-aside food to complete the meal. Having finished eating, one should return silently to the dwelling.
If one enters a village for alms at the very end, one should return as soon as food is obtained and bring it to the place where the meal is to be taken.
If much food has been obtained, one should first set aside a portion.
If one has eaten enough, one should eat; if not yet satisfied, one may take what was previously set aside to eat until full.

If there are leftovers, one should give them to a beggar or a non-human being. One should wash the eating vessels and return them to their original places; likewise, the bedding, water vessels, foot-washing vessels, and sitting mats should be returned to their original places, and the dining area should be swept clean.
If one sees that a water vessel or a foot-washing basin is empty, if one is able to lift it, one should immediately carry it back.

If one cannot lift it, one should beckon a companion with the hand and together carry the vessel back to its original place. Then, returning silently to one's own room, one should not speak on account of this matter, thinking: "In this way, we shall be able to dwell in peace and comfort, and shall not suffer for lack of food and drink. Thus was the rule established.

From this day forward, it is permitted to seek formal authorization provided one possesses five qualities.

What are these five? One must know the proper time and not an improper time; speak according to reality and not with falsehood; speak what is beneficial and not what is unbeneficial; speak with gentleness and not with harshness; and act with a mind of loving-kindness and not with anger.

Those six groups of bhikṣus lacked the five qualities within themselves, while other pure bhikṣus were fully endowed with the five qualities; when those others sought permission from the six groups of bhikṣus, the six groups of bhikṣus did not grant it.
The bhikṣus went to inform the Buddha of these circumstances, and the Buddha said:

At that time, the group of six bhikṣus would depart after requesting permission from others, or they would leave their residence immediately after granting permission to others.
The bhikṣus reported this matter to the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"One should not depart after requesting permission from others and having received it, nor should one depart immediately after granting permission to others."
"From this day forward, I allow you to make a formal agreement with someone and not depart.

Yet the group of six bhikṣus would make an agreement with another and then depart themselves; or they would make an agreement with another and then depart again. The bhikṣus reported this matter to the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"One should not make an agreement with another and then depart oneself; one should not make an agreement with another and then depart again."

From this time forward, it is permitted to perform the *pravāraṇā* at the conclusion of the rainy season retreat; it is also permitted to withhold the *pravāraṇā*, but one should not seek formal permission to do so.
Why? Because the *pravāraṇā* itself constitutes such permission.
The bhikṣus thought to themselves: "The Buddha has permitted the bhikṣus to perform the *pravāraṇā* ceremony.
Consequently, the bhikṣus performed the *pravāraṇā* all at once, resulting in a great commotion. The bhikṣus reported this matter to the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"One should not perform the *pravāraṇā* ceremony all at once.
From now on, it is permitted for each person to perform the *pravāraṇā* individually.

The bhikṣus did not seek the proper order and performed the *pravāraṇā* according to their own whims; consequently, the senior monk (*sthavira*) became utterly exhausted. The bhikṣus reported this matter to the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"One should not perform the *pravāraṇā* (invitation to point out faults) according to one's own will; rather, one should perform the *pravāraṇā* following the senior monks (*sthavira*).
It is permitted to appoint a person to receive the *pravāraṇā* through a formal motion and announcement (*jñapti-dvitīya-karman*).
If a person possesses five qualities, they should not be appointed as the recipient of the *pravāraṇā*: [list of five qualities follows]."
If one is motivated by affection, or by hatred, or by fear, or by delusion, or lacks knowledge of whether the *pravāraṇā* has been performed or not yet performed—
one who possesses these five qualities should not be appointed to receive the *pravāraṇā*.
One who possesses five qualities should be appointed as the person to receive the *prātimokṣa* (invitation to admonish):
one who is not partial, not angry, not fearful, not deluded, and who knows whether the invitation has been completed or not.
One who possesses these five qualities should be appointed to receive the *pravāraṇā*.
Such a capable person should be appointed—whether it be a senior elder (*sthavira*), a junior elder, one who recites the Vinaya, or one who does not recite the Vinaya.
Regarding the formal act (*karmavācanā*) for one who is capable, the motion with a second proclamation (*jñapti-dvitīya-karman*) should be made as follows:
"May the venerable Saṃgha listen!
If the time is right for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha permits it, let the Saṃgha appoint the monk so-and-so to be the person who receives the invitation to confession (*pravāraṇā-grāhaka*)."
The motion is thus made: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
The Saṃgha appoints the bhikṣu so-and-so as the person to receive the invitation to admonish."

"Whichever elders approve of appointing the bhikṣu [Name] as the one who receives the invitation to confess faults (pravāraṇā-grāhaka), let them remain silent; whoever does not approve, let them speak.

"The Sangha has finished approving the appointment of the bhikṣu [Name] as the one who receives the invitation to confess faults. Since the Sangha approves by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld."
At that time, while the bhikṣus were performing the *pravāraṇā* while remaining seated on their cushions, the bhikṣus reported this matter to the Buddha. The Buddha said:
"One should not perform the *pravāraṇā* while remaining seated on one's cushion; it is permitted to rise from one's seat, kneel with the right knee on the ground, and perform the *pravāraṇā*."
At that time, when the Elder rose from his seat for the *pravāraṇā*, the entire Saṃgha remained seated for the *pravāraṇā*. The Buddha said:
"If the Elder rises from his seat and kneels with lowered body (*prāñjali*), the entire Saṃgha should likewise rise from their seats and kneel with lowered bodies."

At that time, after the senior monk (sthavira) had finished the *pravāraṇā*, he knelt with his right knee on the ground; this continued until the entire Saṃgha had finished the *pravāraṇā*. The senior monk became utterly exhausted. The bhikṣus reported this matter to the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"I allow you to sit down again once the *pravāraṇā* has concluded."
At that time, the group of six bhikṣus thought to themselves:
"We shall hold our private conversation during the *pravāraṇā*; perhaps that bhikṣu will perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against us or obstruct our *pravāraṇā*."
The bhikṣus went to inform the Buddha of this matter, and the Buddha said:
"You should not harbor such a thought as:
'I shall speak in secret during the *pravāraṇā*, for fear that other bhikṣus might perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against me or obstruct my *pravāraṇā*.'"
"One should perform the *pravāraṇā* clearly so that others may hear it.
Those monks of the group of six then thought:
"We shall perform the *pravāraṇā* very quickly, for we fear that other monks will perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against us or obstruct our *pravāraṇā*."
The bhikṣus informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"You should not think: 'I shall perform the *pravāraṇā* very quickly, for fear that other bhikṣus might perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against me or obstruct my *pravāraṇā*.'"
"From this day forward, it is permitted to perform the *pravāraṇā* at one's own leisure after the *varṣā* retreat has concluded. Those monks of the group of six thought:
"We shall perform the *pravāraṇā* with a single recitation, lest other monks perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against us or obstruct our *pravāraṇā*."
The bhikṣus informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"You should not think: 'I shall perform the *pravāraṇā* by speaking only once, fearing that other bhikṣus will perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against me or obstruct my *pravāraṇā*.'"
Those six groups of bhikṣus thought to themselves:
"We shall state our invitation for criticism a second time, fearing that other bhikṣus might perform a formal act (karmavācanā) against us or obstruct our invitation."
The bhikṣus informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
“You should not think thus:
‘I shall state my invitation to criticism (pravāraṇā) a second time, fearing that other bhikṣus might perform a formal act (karmavācanā) against me or obstruct my invitation.’”
“From this day forward, I permit the bhikṣus to perform the *pravāraṇā* by reciting three times.

At that time, the group of six bhikṣus performed the *pravāraṇā* with their robes tucked up over one shoulder, performed the *pravāraṇā* with their robes wrapped around their necks, performed the *pravāraṇā* with their heads covered, performed the *pravāraṇā* with their robes draped over both shoulders, performed the *pravāraṇā* wearing leather sandals, and performed the *pravāraṇā* either sitting on the ground or sitting on beds. The bhikṣus went and informed the Buddha, who said:

“One should not perform the *pravāraṇā* with the robe tucked up, wrapped around the neck, covering the head, draped over both shoulders, while wearing leather sandals, or while sitting on the ground or sitting on a bed.”

From this day forward, it is permitted for the bhikṣus to bare their right shoulders, remove their leather sandals, kneel with their right knees on the ground, join their palms, and speak these words:
"Venerable Saṃgha, today is the day of the *pravāraṇā*; I, the bhikṣu [Name], also perform the *pravāraṇā*."
"If you see, hear, or suspect a transgression, O virtuous elders, please speak to me out of compassion.
If I see a transgression, I shall confess it according to the Dharma.
Thus he speaks a second and a third time.
At that time, there was a sick bhikṣu who, having bared his right shoulder, removed his leather sandals, and knelt with palms joined, suddenly found his long-standing illness exacerbated.
The bhikṣus informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"From this day forward, I permit a sick bhikṣu to receive the *pravāraṇā* according to what is convenient for his body."

At that time, in a certain residence, the monks were performing the *pravāraṇā*. A monk was outside the hall where the precepts were being recited; when the monks had finished their *pravāraṇā*, they rose and went outside.
A bhikṣu asked, "Venerable sir, where have you gone? Did you not perform the *pravāraṇā*? He replied:
"I have already finished the *pravāraṇā*.
"From where have you come? He replied:
"I am outside the Poṣadha hall," the bhikṣus reported to the Buddha. The Buddha said:

"From this day forward, during the time of the Pravāraṇā ceremony, one should not remain outside the Poṣadha hall. One should listen to whether those sitting nearby have arrived or not; having first made an announcement, one may then perform the Pravāraṇā."
He makes this announcement:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
Today the community of monks performs the *pravāraṇā*."
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, may the Saṃgha, being in harmony, perform the *pravāraṇā*.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
Having made this motion, they perform the *pravāraṇā*.

The group of six bhikṣus performed the *pravāraṇā* (invitation for criticism) in an illegal manner with a divided assembly, in an illegal manner with a united assembly, and in a legal manner with a divided assembly.
The bhikṣus reported this to the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"One should not perform the *pravāraṇā* in an illegal manner with a divided assembly, nor in an illegal manner with a united assembly, nor in a legal manner with a divided assembly."
There are four kinds of *pravāraṇā*:

if a bhikṣu performs the *pravāraṇā* in an illegal manner with a divided assembly; the *pravāraṇā* in an illegal manner with a united assembly; the *pravāraṇā* in a legal manner with a divided assembly; and the *pravāraṇā* in a legal manner with a united assembly.

If a bhikṣu performs a *pravāraṇā* that is both illegal and conducted by a divided assembly; or an illegal *pravāraṇā* conducted by a united assembly; or a legal *pravāraṇā* conducted by a divided assembly—in such cases, the *pravāraṇā* is not valid.
“The *pravāraṇā* performed through the harmony of the Dharma should be conducted in this manner; this is the *pravāraṇā* that I authorize.
At that time, during the *pravāraṇā*, people who had entered the rains retreat both early and late were living together in different residences, and they did not know what to do.
The monks asked the Buddha: "Should the *pravāraṇā* be performed according to the preceding *varṣā* or the subsequent *varṣā*? The Buddha said:

"The *pravāraṇā* should be performed according to where the *sthavira* is located. Whether the *sthavira* has entered the rains retreat earlier or later, the *pravāraṇā* should follow those who have resided there for a longer time."

"Those who have resided there for a long time may also observe either the earlier *varṣā* (the first retreat) or the later *varṣā* (the second retreat); the *pravāraṇā* should be performed according to whichever is more numerous.
At that time, the bhikṣus wished to perform the *pravāraṇā* on either the fourteenth or the fifteenth day. The Buddha said:
"I allow you to perform the *pravāraṇā* in this manner; however, if the king changes the date, it should be conducted according to the time."
The bhikṣus did not know whether the *pravāraṇā* was to be held today or tomorrow.
The bhikṣus went and informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"From this day forward, I allow that at the time of the morning meal or the midday meal, the *sthavira* shall make a proclamation:”
"Today the Saṃgha shall perform the Pravāraṇā.
Yet they did not know at what time it should be used.
The Buddha said:

"Listen for the signs that it is time to perform [the *pravāraṇā*]: whether the *ghanṭī* is struck, or the *bherī* drum is beaten, or the conch is blown, or smoke is raised, or the shadow is measured, or the proclamation is made:
'The time for the *pravāraṇā* has now arrived.'"

When the group of six bhikṣus heard that the Buddha had permitted the *pravāraṇā*, they went to separate rooms and held their *pravāraṇā* in a different assembly together with their same preceptors (*upādhyāya*), teachers (*ācārya*), close companions, and those with whom they shared mutual affection.
The bhikṣus informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"One should not perform the *pravāraṇā* separately in a private room with one's own upādhyāya, ācārya, close fellow-student, or a dear friend."
"From this day forward, you shall perform the *pravāraṇā* in harmony in one place.
The bhikṣus did not know where they should perform the *pravāraṇā*, so they informed the Buddha. The Buddha said:
"One may perform the *pravāraṇā* at the place where the *poṣadha* is held.

At that time, there were many bhikṣus who, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, were traveling along a road in a non-village area, in a forest hermitage (*araṇya*), and in a place where the boundaries had not yet been established.
The bhikṣus thought to themselves:
"The Buddha has instructed us to perform the *pravāraṇā* in harmony; how should we proceed?
The bhikṣus informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"If many bhikṣus, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, are traveling on a road in a place that is neither a village nor an *araṇya* and where the boundaries have not yet been established:
it is well if those bhikṣus are able to perform the *pravāraṇā* in harmony."

If they cannot achieve harmony, they should, according to their shared upādhyāya or ācārya, or according to those with whom they are intimate and of like mind, move to another location, establish a small boundary (*kṣudrasīmā*), and perform the *pravāraṇā*.
The *jñapti-dvitīya-karman* (formal act consisting of one motion and one proclamation) for establishing a small boundary (*kṣudra-sīmā*) should be performed as follows.

An appropriate person—whether an elder (*sthavira*), a junior monk (*anusthavira*), one who recites the Vinaya, or one who does not recite the Vinaya, provided they are capable of performing the *karman*—should make the following motion:
"May the venerable Saṃgha listen!

The seats for the bhikṣus are already full; up to these seats occupied by the bhikṣus, if it is the proper time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha permits, let the Saṃgha establish a small boundary (sīmā) at this place.
The motion is thus made: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
Within the seating area of these bhikṣus, the Saṃgha shall establish a small boundary (sīmā) at this place."

"Whichever elders approve of the Sangha establishing a small boundary (sīmā) within this area defined by the seating places of these monks, let them remain silent; whoever does not approve, let them speak.

"The Sangha has approved the establishment of the small boundary within this area defined by the seating places of these monks. Since the Sangha is silent, it is thus held that this matter is settled."
At that time, the bhikṣu departed without relinquishing the boundary; the other bhikṣus were displeased and immediately went to inform the Buddha.
The Buddha said:
"One should not depart without relinquishing the boundary; one should relinquish the boundary and only then depart."

One should perform the relinquishment in this manner: having appointed a capable person through a *jñapti-dvitīya-karman*—whether it be a senior monk (*sthavira*), a junior monk (*anusthavira*), one who recites the Vinaya, or one who does not recite the Vinaya, provided they are capable of performing the *karman*—one should make the following formal motion (*jñapti*):
"May the venerable Saṃgha listen!..."
"Venerable sirs, listen! If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let the Saṃgha dissolve this small boundary at this location.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*). Venerable Saṃgha, listen!"
"Venerable sirs, let the Saṃgha mark off this small boundary within the seating area of these bhikṣus.
Those elders who consent to the Saṃgha marking off this small boundary within the seating area of these bhikṣus should remain silent; those who do not consent should speak."
“The Saṃgha has already consented; the minor boundary has been dissolved at the seating places of these bhikṣus. Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.”
The *Dharmaguptaka-vinaya*, Fascicle 37 and two-thirds of Fascicle 38.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Buddhayaśas of Kapiśī during the Yao Qin dynasty.
Translated by Zhu Fonian and others. Part Three:
The Pravāraṇā-khaṇḍaka, Second Section. At that time, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, there was a certain monastery where a single bhikṣu resided. He thought to himself:
"The World-Honored One has given this instruction: 'One should gather together in one place and perform the *pravāraṇā* collectively.'"
"What should I do? He then informed the bhikṣus, who in turn informed the Buddha. The Buddha said:

"On the day of the *pravāraṇā*, if there is a single bhikṣu staying in a different location, he should go to the place where the *poṣadha* is to be recited; he should sweep and sprinkle it, prepare the seats, provide water vessels, provide foot-washing implements, light lamps, and prepare the *śalākā* for the visiting bhikṣus."
If five or more visiting bhikṣus arrive, one should perform a formal motion (*jñapti-karman*) to appoint a person to receive the invitation to confess faults (*pravāraṇā*).
If there are four persons, they may perform the mutual invitation to confess faults by saying:
"Today the Saṃgha performs the *pravāraṇā*; I, the bhikṣu so-and-so, also perform the *pravāraṇā* and am pure."
The second and third [monks] should also speak in this manner.
If there are three or two persons, they should likewise perform the *pravāraṇā* in this way.
If there is only one person, he performs the *pravāraṇā* by mental reflection and verbal declaration:
"Today the Saṃgha performs the *pravāraṇā*; I, bhikṣu so-and-so, am pure regarding the *pravāraṇā*.
The second and third [recitations] are to be spoken in the same manner.
If there are five persons, one may receive the consent (*chanda*), but it is not permitted to formally appoint someone to receive the *pravāraṇā*.
If there are four persons, they may not receive the consent (*chanda*) of a fifth person to perform the mutual *prātimokṣa* ceremony.
If there are three persons, they may not receive the consent of a fourth person to perform the mutual *prātimokṣa* ceremony.
If there are two persons, they may not receive the *chanda* (consent) of a third person to perform the *pravāraṇā* (invitation to admonish) with one another.
If there is only one person, he may not receive the *chanda* of a second person; he must perform the *pravāraṇā* through mental reflection (*manasikāra*).
At that time, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, the community of monks gathered, intending to perform the *pravāraṇā*.
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
"Be silent today; the community of monks shall perform the *pravāraṇā*."
Other bhikṣus informed the Buddha, saying:
“There is a sick bhikṣu who has not come.
The Buddha said:
"Regarding the granting of the *pravāraṇā* and the entrusting of the *pravāraṇā*:
one should address the sick person as follows:
'I grant you the *pravāraṇā*.'"
If one says: "I tell you to exercise your *prātimokṣa* at will," or if one says:
"Grant me the *pravāraṇā*. If one grants the *pravāraṇā* by moving the body or by speaking the *pravāraṇā* formula at length, this is called granting the *pravāraṇā*.
If one does not move the body nor speak with the mouth, the granting of the *pravāraṇā* is not accomplished; one should grant the *pravāraṇā* again.
If a bhikṣu who has been entrusted with a charge goes to the place of a sick person and that person passes away; or if he goes beyond the boundary; or if he abandons the path;
or if he goes to the dwelling place of non-Buddhists; or if he joins the faction of those who have split the Saṃgha;
or if he goes to the site of a formal ordination (sīmā); or if the dawn appears; or if he himself declares that he has committed a pārājika offense; or if he commits a bhikṣu-offense.
A bhikṣuṇī; one who has entered the path with a thieving mind; one who has returned from among the non-Buddhists; a eunuch; one who has killed his father or mother;
one who has killed an arhat; one who has caused a schism in the Saṃgha; one who has maliciously shed the blood of a Buddha;
one who is a non-human (amanuṣya); one who is an animal; one who possesses both sexual organs; or one who acts on behalf of another.

If one has been accused, or if one has been expelled, or if one is subject to expulsion—if one gives the *pravāraṇā* (invitation for criticism) to such persons as these, the entrustment of the *pravāraṇā* is not valid; one should instead give it to another person.

Whether on the way or upon arriving at the Saṃgha, if such circumstances arise—such as the Saṃgha performing the *karmavācanā* for one who does not acknowledge their offense, or the *karmavācanā* for one who does not repent their offense, or the *karmavācanā* for one who does not renounce an evil view—the *poṣadha* (self-examination) by proxy is not validly established; one should instead grant it to another person.

If one does not speak because of sleep, or because one has entered meditative concentration, or due to forgetfulness or error, or if one has not intentionally [failed to speak] by the time of the *pravāraṇā*, this constitutes a formal entrustment for the *pravāraṇā*.
Upon arriving, if one intentionally does not speak, it is a *duṣkṛta* offense.

If one is able to act in this manner, it is well; if one cannot do so, they should support and escort the sick bhikṣu away—whether by means of a rope bed, a wooden bed, or by carrying him on a cloth stretcher—to the place where the *pravāraṇā* is to be held.
Those bhikṣus should think:
"If we carry this sick bhikṣu away, his illness may increase or he may die.
The Saṃgha should all come to where the patient is and perform the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*.

If there are many bhikṣus who have gathered in one place due to illness, that is well; if they are unable to do so, the bhikṣus should go outside the boundary to perform the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*, and they must not perform the *pravāraṇā* as a separate assembly.

At that time, there was a bhikṣu who, having received the entrustment for the *pravāraṇā*, passed away, or ceased his religious life, or went to the boundary of the precept-platform (*sīmā*), or until the appearance of the dawn; the other bhikṣus thought to themselves:
"Has he lost the entrustment for the *pravāraṇā*?"
The Buddha said, "It is lost.

At that time, there was a bhikṣu who had entrusted his *pravāraṇā* (invitation for criticism). Two paths were cut off due to the perils of bandits, tigers, wolves, and lions; the waters swelled greatly; and the path within the boundary was blocked, making it impossible for him to go outside the boundary to bring back the entrusted *pravāraṇā*.
The bhikṣus had this thought: "Does this not constitute a failure to inform [the preceptor] before the *pravāraṇā*?
The Buddha said:
"It is not lost.

From this time forward, if a bhikṣu who has received the entrustment for the *pravāraṇā* encounters a threat to life or a threat to his pure conduct, and there is no path within the boundary, he is permitted to come from outside the boundary bringing the entrusted *pravāraṇā*. I declare that the entrusted *pravāraṇā* is not lost."
The bhikṣus, having received the invitation from one person, were apprehensive and did not dare to receive further invitations; they immediately informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"I allow you to receive them."

At that time, a bhikṣu had received the invitation for the *pravāraṇā* from two people; out of caution and fear, he did not dare to accept further invitations. He immediately informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"I permit you to accept them."

At that time, a bhikṣu accepted the invitation for the *pravāraṇā* from three people who had entrusted it to him, but out of caution he did not dare to accept the invitation from four people. He immediately informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"I permit you to accept them; you should accept as many as you are able to remember by their names."

If you remember the name, you should state the name; if you do not remember the name, you should state the clan; or you may describe their physical appearance; or you may say, "I have received the formal authorization (*anujñā*) for the *pravāraṇā* from many bhikṣus."

When that [monk] was about to give his consent for a formal act of the Saṃgha according to the Dharma and announce his invitation for the *pravāraṇā*, a young bhikṣu did not know how to perform the *pravāraṇā* and informed the other bhikṣus.
The bhikṣus reported this to the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"From now on, he should be instructed by his *upādhyāya* or *ācārya*. If they are prone to forgetfulness and fail to remember, one who is giving the *pravāraṇā* should be made to instruct him."
"If you should again forget it intentionally, you ought to recite it together, phrase by phrase.
When the bhikṣus had received the entrustment for the *pravāraṇā* and a matter arose, the bhikṣus informed the Buddha. The Buddha said:
"From this day forward, I allow you to further transfer it to another person. It should be transferred in this manner:"

"I have received the authorization for the *pravāraṇā* from many bhikṣus. Now that I have business, I shall grant my consent (*chanda*) on their behalf, as well as grant my own consent; regarding the legal matters of the Saṃgha, I grant my consent and declare my *pravāraṇā*."

After that bhikṣu had completed the transmission of his consent and returned to rest, he became apprehensive, thinking: "I have already finished transmitting my authorization for the *pravāraṇā*, yet I do not know what to do now."
The bhikṣus went to inform the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"If the matter has been resolved, you should go; if it has not been resolved, you should be dealt with according to the Dharma.
At that time, the group of six bhikṣus thought to themselves:
"I will not go to the place of the *pravāraṇā*, for fear that they might perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against me or obstruct my *pravāraṇā*.
The bhikṣus reported this to the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"One should not entertain such a thought."
"I shall not go to the place of the *pravāraṇā* ceremony, for I fear that the bhikṣus will perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against me or obstruct my *pravāraṇā*.
The same applies if one does not go to the *pravāraṇā* ceremony because of close personal ties or friendship.
At that time, the group of six bhikṣus thought to themselves:
"If we do not sit at the place where the *pravāraṇā* is held, we fear that the other bhikṣus will perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against us or obstruct our *pravāraṇā*."
The bhikṣus went and informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"You should not think thus:
'I will not sit at the place of the *pravāraṇā*, for fear that the bhikṣus will perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against me or obstruct my *pravāraṇā*.'"
"If it is for the sake of a close friend or relative, it is also like this. He then thinks:
"If I go there and do not speak [of my own] *pravāraṇā*, I fear that the bhikṣus will perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against me or obstruct my *pravāraṇā*."
The bhikṣus informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"You should not entertain such a thought as this:
'I shall go there and not speak of the *pravāraṇā*, fearing that the bhikṣus will perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against me or obstruct my *pravāraṇā*.'"
"If it is for the sake of one's close friends and relatives, it is also like this.

At that time, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, there was a different residence where the community of monks, being in harmony, wished to perform the *pravāraṇā*. Hearing that bandits were coming, they became terrified, left their seats, and departed, ultimately not performing the *pravāraṇā*.
The bhikṣus reported this matter to the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"It is permitted.
If any of the eight difficulties should arise, it is permitted to perform the *pravāraṇā* in an abbreviated manner."
The difficulties therein are:

the difficulty of kings, the difficulty of thieves, the difficulty of fire, the difficulty of water, the difficulty of illness, the difficulty of humans, the difficulty of non-humans, and the difficulty of venomous insects.
Regarding the matters therein:
if the assembly of monks is large and the seating is cramped, or if many people are ill, the *pravāraṇā* should be performed briefly.
If the assembly of monks is large, or if the dwellings are few, or if it is raining, the *pravāraṇā* should be performed briefly.

If the night of the poṣadha has passed too long, or if there is a matter of dispute, or if Abhidharma is being discussed, or if Vinaya analogies are being analyzed, or if the night of preaching the Dharma has already lasted a long time, yet the Saṃgha has not yet risen and the dawn light has not yet appeared, one should perform the *pravāraṇā* through a formal ritual motion (*karmavācanā*).
Having received the formal authorization (*anujñā*) for the *pravāraṇā* from another, one must not wait until the appearance of the dawn light.
If the dawn light appears, the *pravāraṇā* by means of a formal ritual (*karmavācanā*) cannot be performed. The monks spoke as follows:
"In times of difficulty, we have briefly explained the *pravāraṇā*, yet the period of difficulty is still far off; therefore, we may explain the *pravāraṇā* in detail.
That bhikṣu should then explain the *pravāraṇā* in detail; if he does not explain it in detail, he should be dealt with according to the Dharma.
The bhikṣus spoke thus:

"Since the *pravāraṇā* is being recited in brief due to difficult circumstances, and as these difficulties are not far off, we shall not be able to perform the *pravāraṇā* with the three formal utterances; therefore, we shall perform the *pravāraṇā* by reciting it twice."
He should then repeat the invitation for self-examination (*pravāraṇā*). If he does not repeat it, he should be dealt with according to the Dharma.
The monks should speak thus:

"The invitation for self-examination was abbreviated due to difficult circumstances; now that the difficult circumstances are imminent, it is not possible to repeat the invitation for self-examination, but one may perform the invitation for self-examination once."
That bhikṣu should then perform the *pravāraṇā* with a single recitation; if he does not do so, he should be dealt with according to the Dharma. The bhikṣus spoke thus:

"Because of difficult circumstances, we have performed the *pravāraṇā* in brief. Since the difficult circumstances are imminent, we cannot perform the *pravāraṇā* with a single recitation; we should allow each other to perform the *pravāraṇā* by means of three words."

The bhikṣus should immediately make the formal announcement (*jñapti*), and each should perform the *pravāraṇā* (invitation to admonish) with three statements. The announcement should be made as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
If the time is right for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let the Saṃgha now each perform the *pravāraṇā* with three statements."
"Thus it is announced.
Having thus announced, they each perform the *pravāraṇā* (invitation to admonish) with three statements.
It is the same for two statements or one statement.
The bhikṣus spoke thus:

"In times of difficulty, we each perform the *pravāraṇā* with three statements together; when difficulties are imminent, we cannot perform the *pravāraṇā* with three statements together, nor can we perform the formal announcement (*jñapti*)."
"That bhikṣu should immediately depart because of this difficult situation.
At that time, there was a bhikṣu in another residence who had committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; he did not know what to do.
He addressed the bhikṣus.
The bhikṣus went and informed the Buddha, who said:

"If a bhikṣu commits a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense while residing in another dwelling place, and that bhikṣu is subject to the *paryuṣaṇā* (concealment) penance, then the *paryuṣaṇā* should be granted; once the *paryuṣaṇā-karman* has been completed, he should then perform the *pravāraṇā*."
One who should be granted the *mānatva* penance must be granted it; once the formal act (*karmavācanā*) for granting the *mānatva* penance is completed, one should perform the *pravāraṇā*.
One who should be granted the *tad-ahar-kalpa* (penance of that very day) must be granted it; once the formal act for granting the *tad-ahar-kalpa* is completed, one should perform the *pravāraṇā*.

"One should grant rehabilitation from the offense; one ought to grant rehabilitation from the offense; once the formal act (*karmavācanā*) of granting rehabilitation is completed, one should perform the *pravāraṇā*.

At that time, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, there was a bhikṣu residing in another monastery who had committed a *pāyattika* offense; some said he had committed a *pāyattika*, while others said he had committed a *pratideśanīya*.
They spoke thus: "What should we do? and immediately informed the bhikṣus.
The bhikṣus informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:

"If, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, there is a bhikṣu residing in another monastery who has committed a *pāyattika* offense, and the bhikṣus therein either say he has committed a *pāyattika* or say he has committed a *pratideśanīya*."
If one knows that [the person] has committed a *pāyattika* offense, one should immediately take that person to a secluded place and have them speak.

Regarding a *pratideśanīya* offense, having instructed the person to confess in a place where they can be seen but not heard, one should go to the bhikṣu who committed the *pratideśanīya* offense and say:
"I have already instructed that offending bhikṣu to confess."
"Having performed such expedients as these, one should then perform the *pravāraṇā*.
At that time, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, there was a bhikṣu residing in another location who had committed a *sthūlātyaya*.
Some bhikṣus said he had committed a *sthūlātyaya*, while others said he had committed a *pārājika*.

Regarding those said to have committed a *sthūlātyaya*, they were all widely learned, versed in the *Āgamas* and *Abhidharma*, and upholders of the Vinaya; they were bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs with many acquaintances, as well as laymen (*upāsaka*), laywomen (*upāsikā*), kings, ministers, and various non-Buddhist śramaṇas and brahmins.

The bhikṣu who is said to have committed a pārājika offense was also one of great learning, well-versed in the Āgamas and Abhidharma, and a master of the Vinaya; he was furthermore a bhikṣu with many acquaintances, including bhikṣuṇīs, śramaṇas, and brahmins.
The bhikṣus spoke thus:

"If the *pravāraṇā* is held today, there will surely be disputes among the Saṃgha; perhaps it will lead to a schism in the Saṃgha, or give rise to defilements that pollute the Saṃgha, causing the Saṃgha to become divided."
"What should we do? They immediately informed the bhikṣus, and the bhikṣus went to inform the Buddha. The Buddha said:
"If, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, there is a bhikṣu residing in another monastery who has committed a *sthūlātyaya* offense,
and the bhikṣus therein either say he has committed a *sthūlātyaya* or say he has committed a *pārājika*."

Those who speak of committing a *sthūlātyaya* offense are all those of great learning, who are versed in the *Āgamas* and the *Abhidharma*, who uphold the Vinaya, and who have many acquaintances among monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, as well as kings, ministers, and various non-Buddhist śramaṇas and brahmins.

Regarding those who have committed a *pārājika* offense, these bhikṣus were also learned, having mastered the *Āgamas*, the *Abhidharma*, and the Vinaya; furthermore, they had many acquaintances among bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, as well as among śramaṇas and brahmins.
The bhikṣus spoke thus:

"If we hold the *pravāraṇā* today, there will surely be disputes among the Saṃgha; perhaps it will lead to a schism in the Saṃgha, or give rise to the dust and filth of the Saṃgha that defiles the community, causing the Saṃgha to become divided."
"If one fears that it would cause a schism in the Saṃgha, one should not perform the *pravāraṇā* on that very day, but should delay the *pravāraṇā* for a short time.

At the time of the *pravāraṇā*, the group of six bhikṣus, hearing that the Buddha had permitted the postponement of the *pravāraṇā*, immediately obstructed pure bhikṣus from performing the *pravāraṇā*. The bhikṣus went and informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"One should not obstruct the *pravāraṇā* of pure bhikṣus; if one obstructs them, it is as if one has not obstructed them at all."
If one objects to that which is groundless and lacks a formal act, this is called not obstructing the *pravāraṇā*.
If one objects to that which is grounded and possesses a formal act, this is called obstructing the *pravāraṇā*.
If one objects to that which is groundless but possesses other [grounds] and lacks a formal act, this is called not obstructing the *pravāraṇā*.
If one objects on grounds that are unfounded and with a remainder, it is called obstructing the *prātimokṣa* ceremony.
If one objects on grounds that are unfounded and without a remainder, it is called not obstructing the *prātimokṣa* ceremony.
If one objects on the grounds that there is no root [of authority] and no other agent, this is called obstructing the *pravāraṇā*.
Since the *pravāraṇā* by means of the three utterances has not yet been declared, if one objects to it, this is called not obstructing the *pravāraṇā*.
When the invitation for self-examination (*pravāraṇā*) has been completed after three recitations, if one obstructs the self-examination, this is called "not obstructing the self-examination.
When the invitation for self-examination is being recited for the third time, if one obstructs the self-examination, this is called "obstructing the self-examination."
The same applies to the first and second proclamations.

Regarding one who obstructs the *pravāraṇā* (invitation to admonish), if their bodily action is impure, their verbal action is impure, their mental action is impure, they lack wisdom and are not discerning, they do not know how to ask questions, and they are unable to answer, the other bhikṣus should say to this bhikṣu: "Stop!"
"Elder! There is no need to raise this matter of dispute; do not heed the words of this bhikṣu.
Then they should proceed with the *pravāraṇā*.

If, when the *pravāraṇā* is being suspended, a person’s bodily action is pure but their verbal and mental actions are impure, lacking wisdom and clarity, not knowing how to ask questions, and unable to answer, other bhikṣus should say to this bhikṣu: "Stop!..."
"Elder! There is no need to raise this matter of dispute; do not heed the words of this bhikṣu.
Then they should proceed with the *pravāraṇā*.

If a person who obstructs the *pravāraṇā* has purity of body and speech but impurity of mental action—being without wisdom, lacking clarity, not knowing how to ask questions, and unable to answer—other bhikṣus should say to this bhikṣu: "Stop! [Do not obstruct the *pravāraṇā*]."
"Elder! There is no need to raise this matter of dispute; do not heed the words of this bhikṣu.
Then one should proceed with the *pravāraṇā*.

If a person who obstructs the *pravāraṇā* is pure in their actions of body, speech, and mind, possesses clear intelligence, and is capable of both questioning and answering, other bhikṣus should say to that bhikṣu:
"For what reason do you obstruct this bhikṣu’s *pravāraṇā*?"
"Is it because of a transgression of the precepts that one is excluded, or because of the destruction of right view, or because of the destruction of proper deportment?
If he answers, "It is because of a transgression of the precepts that one is excluded."
One should ask:
"What kind of precept have you violated?
If they say they have violated a *pārājika*, a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*, or a *sthūlātyaya*, this is called "violation of the precepts."
If one says:
"It is not because of the breaking of the precepts that they are barred, but because of the breaking of right view," one should ask:
"What is the destruction of views? If one says:
"The sixty-two views and all false views."
This is called "corrupting views.
If one says:
"It is not because of corrupting views, but because of corrupting the majestic deportment that it is prohibited."
One should ask:
"In what way does one violate the rules of decorum? If he says:
"To commit a *pāyattika*, a *pratideśanīya*, a *dukkaṭa*, or an improper speech"—
this is called the violation of decorum.
One should further ask:
"For what reason do you obstruct another's *pravāraṇā*?
Is it because of what you have seen, heard, or suspected? If one says:
If they say, "Because I see," one should ask: "What do you see?"
"How do you see? For what reason do you see?
Furthermore, by what causes and conditions does that bhikṣu cause you to see?"
Where do you dwell? Where does he dwell? What do you see?
Is it an offense of pārājika, saṃghāvaśeṣa, pāyattika, prātideśanīya, sthūlātyaya, duṣkṛta, or dubbhāsita?
If they say, "I did not see it, but because I heard of it," one should ask:
"What have you heard? How did you hear it?
From whom did you hear it?"
Did you hear this from a bhikṣu?
Or did you hear it from a bhikṣuṇī, an upāsaka, or an upāsikā?
What matter was heard to have been transgressed?
"Is it a *pārājika*, a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*, or even a mere *durbhāṣita*? If he says:
"I did not hear it; it was because of doubt."
One should ask:
"In what matter do you have doubt?
How do you doubt?"
From whom did you hear it that this doubt arose?
Was it from a bhikṣu, a bhikṣuṇī, an upāsaka, or an upāsikā? What is the matter concerning which you have doubts?
"Is it because of doubt regarding a *pārājika*, a *saṃghāvaśeṣa*, or even a mere *durbhāṣita*?

If the person who obstructs the *pravāraṇā* cannot answer a wise person, and if they have obstructed it on the grounds of a *pārājika*, the [obstructor] should be given the offense of *saṃghāvaśeṣa*; only then may the Saṃgha perform the *pravāraṇā*.
If one is obstructed by a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, one should be given a *pāyattika* offense, and only then should the Saṃgha perform the *pravāraṇā*.
If one is obstructed by a *pāyattika* offense, one should be given another offense, and only then should the Saṃgha perform the *pravāraṇā*.
If one obstructs [the *pravāraṇā*] on account of other matters, they should be dealt with according to the Dharma, and only then should the Saṃgha perform the *pravāraṇā*.

If the person who obstructs the *pravāraṇā* can provide an answer to those who possess wisdom, and if they obstruct it on account of a *pārājika* offense, they should be expelled (*pravrājana*), and only then should the Saṃgha perform the *pravāraṇā*.
If one is obstructed by a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense, one should be granted parivāsa, or mūlāpakarṣa, or mānāpya, or āvarhaṇa; once these have been granted, one should then perform the pravāraṇā.
If one is obstructed by a *pāyattika* offense, one should perform the *pravāraṇā* after having confessed it.
If one is obstructed by other matters, one should be dealt with according to the Dharma, and only then perform the *pravāraṇā*.
At that time, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, there was a sick bhikṣu residing in a certain monastery who obstructed another sick bhikṣu from performing the *pravāraṇā*. Not knowing what to do,
he informed the other bhikṣus.
The bhikṣus went and informed the Buddha. The Buddha said:
"If, on the day of the *pravāraṇā* at a certain residence, a sick bhikṣu prevents another sick bhikṣu from performing the *pravāraṇā*, that bhikṣu should say to this bhikṣu:
'The Buddha has spoken thus:'"
"Today, one should not obstruct a sick bhikṣu.
One must wait until this illness has been cured; the Elder should speak according to the Dharma.
He too shall speak according to the Dharma; having done so, they may then perform the *pravāraṇā*.
At that time, there was a certain residence where, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, a sick bhikṣu prevented a healthy bhikṣu from performing the *pravāraṇā*. That bhikṣu said to the other bhikṣu:
"Venerable sir!..."
The Buddha spoke thus:
"One must wait until the illness has subsided before speaking according to the Dharma.
They too should speak according to the Dharma; having done so, they may then perform the *pravāraṇā*.
At that time, there was a residence where, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, a healthy bhikṣu obstructed a sick bhikṣu from performing the *pravāraṇā*.
That bhikṣu said to this bhikṣu:
"The Buddha has spoken thus: [text continues]"
"One must wait until the illness has been cured.
The Elder should speak according to the Dharma.
He too shall speak according to the Dharma; having done so, they may then perform the *pravāraṇā*.

At that time, there was another dwelling place where a large number of bhikṣus had entered the rains retreat (*varṣā*). Through diligent practice of the Path, they attained the realization of superior fruits (*viśeṣa-phala*).
They thought to themselves:
"If we were to perform the *pravāraṇā* ceremony today, we would have to move to another location; we fear we may not obtain such bliss again."
"What should we do? They immediately informed the bhikṣus, and the bhikṣus went to report this to the Buddha. The Buddha said:
"If there is a dwelling place where many bhikṣus have entered the rains retreat and, through diligent practice of the Path,
have attained the realization of superior fruits, those bhikṣus might think:
'If we were to perform the *pravāraṇā* ceremony today, we would have to move to another location, and we fear we may not obtain such happiness again.'"
That bhikṣu should immediately make a formal announcement (*jñapti*) to extend the *pravāraṇā*, making the announcement as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
If the time has come for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha consents, let the Saṃgha not perform the *pravāraṇā* today; rather, it shall perform the *pravāraṇā* when the four months are complete."
"Thus it is announced.
One should make such an announcement for the four-month *pravāraṇā*.
At that time, there was another dwelling place where a great number of bhikṣus resided together.
On the day of the *pravāraṇā*, the bhikṣus heard that the bhikṣus at that residence were quarreling and living in discord, and intended to come here for the *pravāraṇā*.
"What should we do? they asked.
He immediately informed the bhikṣus.
The bhikṣus went and reported this to the Buddha, who said:

"If there is a residence where many bhikṣus dwell together, and on the day of the *pravāraṇā* they hear that bhikṣus from another residence are quarreling and living in discord, intending to come here for the *pravāraṇā*."
That bhikṣu should shorten the days for the *pravāraṇā* ceremony by two or three days.
If the *pravāraṇā* was to be on the fifteenth day, it should be shortened to the fourteenth;
if the *pravāraṇā* was to be on the fourteenth day, it should be shortened to the thirteenth.
If one hears that [the monks] are coming today, one should immediately assemble the Saṃgha and perform the *pravāraṇā* quickly.
If one hears that they have already arrived within the boundary (*sīmā*), one should go outside and perform the *pravāraṇā*.

If one hears that they have already entered the monastery, one should prepare bathing implements, a bath bench, a bathing pitcher, a razor for removing impurities, water vessels, clay vessels, cleansing powder, medicinal herbs, and kindle a fire for the Elder; then, invite the Saṃgha to enter the bathhouse.
The resident bhikṣus should emerge from the bathhouse one by one in secret and go outside the boundary to perform the *pravāraṇā*.
If visiting bhikṣus call for the *pravāraṇā*, they should reply:
"We have already completed our *pravāraṇā*."
If resident bhikṣus have already completed their *pravāraṇā*, visiting bhikṣus who attempt to obstruct the *pravāraṇā* may not do so;
however, if resident bhikṣus attempt to obstruct the *pravāraṇā* while visiting bhikṣus are performing it, they may do so.
If one can thus perform it through skillful means, that is well.
If one cannot, that bhikṣu should perform a formal announcement (*jñapti*) for an *adhiṣṭhita-pravāraṇā* (an empowered invitation), making the announcement as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, please listen!"

"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let the Saṃgha not perform the *pravāraṇā* today; we shall perform the *pravāraṇā* on the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight.
This is the formal announcement (*jñapti*). One should make such an announcement to extend the *pravāraṇā*.

If a visiting bhikṣu remains until the fifteenth day of the dark fortnight, the resident bhikṣus should perform the second formal announcement for the *pravāraṇā* of increased authority, making the announcement as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, please listen!..."

"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha not perform the *pravāraṇā* today; rather, the *pravāraṇā* shall be performed on the fifteenth day of the latter half of the month.
Thus should the motion be made.
One should perform this second *pravāraṇā* with increased formality by means of such a motion.
"If the visiting bhikṣus do not depart, the resident bhikṣus should, in accordance with the Dharma and the Vinaya, forcibly bring about a harmonious *pravāraṇā*.

At that time, on the day of *pravāraṇā*, there was a residence where, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, the offense was not recognized and the person [who committed it] was not recognized; however, after the *pravāraṇā* was concluded, the offense was recognized and the person was recognized.
He thought to himself, "What should we do?
and immediately informed the bhikṣus.
The bhikṣus went and informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:

"There is a case where, during the time of the *pravāraṇā* ceremony at a certain residence, one does not recognize the offense nor the person [who committed it], but after the *pravāraṇā* is concluded, one recognizes both the offense and the person."
"If the *pravāraṇā* has concluded, one must not subsequently authorize the formal accusation of another's offense.

At that time, there was a residence where, during the *pravāraṇā*, the offense was not recognized and the person was not recognized, but after the *pravāraṇā* had concluded, both the offense and the person were recognized.
"If the *pravāraṇā* has concluded, one should not subsequently authorize the formal accusation of another's offense.

At that time, there was a different residence where, during the *pravāraṇā*, the offense was recognized but the person [who committed it] was not; after the *pravāraṇā* had concluded, both the offense and the person were recognized.
"If the *pravāraṇā* has been concluded, one should not, based on what was previously heard, raise charges against another for an offense.

At that time, in a certain other residence, on the day of *pravāraṇā*, guest bhikṣus arrived on the fourteenth day while the resident bhikṣus were on the fifteenth day; the bhikṣus did not know what to do.
He then addressed the bhikṣus.
The bhikṣus said to the Buddha, and the Buddha said:

"If there is a residence where, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, a few guest bhikṣus arrive and the guest bhikṣus' [calculation] falls on the fourteenth day while the resident bhikṣus' falls on the fifteenth day, the guest bhikṣus should follow the resident bhikṣus; if they do not follow them, they shall be dealt with according to the Dharma."

If there is a residence where, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, visiting bhikṣus arrive who are equal in number to the resident bhikṣus, and the visiting bhikṣus have completed fourteen days while the resident bhikṣus have completed fifteen days, the visiting bhikṣus should follow the resident bhikṣus; if they do not follow them, they shall be dealt with according to the Dharma.

If, at the time of the *pravāraṇā*, many guest bhikṣus arrive at a residence such that the guest bhikṣus have reached the fourteenth day and the resident bhikṣus have reached the fifteenth day, and the resident bhikṣus are few in number, they should seek reconciliation from the guest bhikṣus.
If they can achieve harmony with them, it is well; if not, the resident bhikṣus should go outside the boundary to perform the *pravāraṇā*.

If on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, guest bhikṣus from another residence arrive in small numbers—such that the guest bhikṣus are on the fifteenth day while the resident bhikṣus are on the fourteenth—the guest bhikṣus, being few, should seek harmony with the resident bhikṣus.
If they can reach an agreement, it is well; if not, the visiting bhikṣus should go outside the boundary to perform the *pravāraṇā*.

If on the day of *pravāraṇā*, visiting bhikṣus from another residence arrive, and if these resident bhikṣus have the fourteenth day while the visiting bhikṣus have the fifteenth day, the visiting bhikṣus should seek agreement with the resident bhikṣus. If they reach an agreement, it is well; if not, the visiting bhikṣus should go outside the boundary to perform the *pravāraṇā*.

If on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, there is another residence where many guest bhikṣus have arrived, and the guest bhikṣus are on the fifteenth day while the resident bhikṣus are on the fourteenth day—and the resident bhikṣus are few—one should follow the guest bhikṣus; if one does not follow them, one shall be dealt with according to the Dharma.
"It is the same for the fifteenth and sixteenth days as well.
At that time, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, the resident bhikṣus of a certain dwelling gathered, intending to perform the *pravāraṇā*.

If it is said that the *pravāraṇā* has been completed, and the entire assembly has not yet risen, or most have not yet risen, or all have already risen, and if the visiting bhikṣus who have arrived are few, they should be granted purity (*śuddhi*); if it is not granted, one must be dealt with according to the Dharma.

At that time, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, when resident bhikṣus were about to perform the *pravāraṇā* and visiting bhikṣus arrived in equal numbers, it was said: "The resident bhikṣus should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they do not perform it, they shall be dealt with according to the Dharma."

When the *pravāraṇā* has concluded, whether the entire assembly has not yet risen, or most have not yet risen, or all have already risen, if visiting *bhikṣus* arrive, the resident *bhikṣus* should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they do not, they shall be dealt with according to the Dharma.

At that time, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, there were resident monks at a certain monastery who wished to perform the *pravāraṇā*. However, many guest monks arrived. At that time, there was a residence where, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, visiting bhikṣus sat down intending to perform the *pravāraṇā*. Few resident bhikṣus arrived; [the rule was: "The senior resident bhikṣus shall perform the *pravāraṇā* at the place where the senior [visitors] perform theirs;

At that time, there was a residence where, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, visiting monks were seated and about to perform the *pravāraṇā*. If the *pravāraṇā* has concluded, whether the entire assembly has not yet risen, or many have not yet risen, or all have already risen, and resident monks arrive, the visiting monks should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they do not act according to the Dharma, it is contrary to the law.

At that time, there was a residence where, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, visiting bhikṣus were seated intending to perform the *pravāraṇā*. Many resident bhikṣus arrived and said, "The visiting bhikṣus should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they do not, they shall be dealt with according to the Dharma."

If the *pravāraṇā* has concluded, whether the entire assembly has not yet risen, or most have not risen, or all have already risen, and many resident monks (*pūrvabhikṣu*) arrive, the visiting monks (*āgantuka-bhikṣu*) should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they do not act according to the Dharma, it is contrary to the law.
It was the same when resident bhikṣus came to other resident bhikṣus, and it was the same when visiting bhikṣus came to other visiting bhikṣus.
At that time, there was a monastery where visiting bhikṣus arrived on the day of the *pravāraṇā*.
The visiting bhikṣus, knowing that the resident bhikṣus had not yet arrived, thought:
"If we have five or more than five people, we may perform the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*."
They then performed the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*.
While the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā* was being performed, some resident monks arrived, and the visiting monks thought to themselves: "What should we do?"
He then informed the bhikṣus.
The bhikṣus reported this to the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"If, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, there is a residence where visiting bhikṣus arrive..."
The visiting bhikṣus, knowing that resident bhikṣus had not yet arrived, thought:
"If we are five or more than five, we may perform the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*."

At that time, there was a residence where, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, visiting monks arrived.
The visiting monks knew that the resident monks had not yet arrived, and [thought]:
"If we are five or more than five, we may perform the formal act (*karmavācanā*) of *pravāraṇā*."
They then performed the *pravāraṇā* by means of a formal act (*karmavācanā*).

When performing the *pravāraṇā* by means of a formal act, if resident monks arrive at that time, the visiting monks should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they do not do so according to the Dharma, it is an offense.

When the *pravāraṇā* has been completed, if the entire assembly has not yet risen, or if many have not yet risen, or if all have already risen, and a resident monk arrives, the visiting monks should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they do not do so according to the Dharma, it is contrary to the law.
At that time, there was a monastery where, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, visiting bhikṣus arrived.
The visiting bhikṣus knew that the resident bhikṣus had not yet arrived, and they thought:
"If we are five or more than five, we may perform the formal act (*karmavācanā*) of *pravāraṇā* together."
They then performed the *kaṭhina* ceremony for the invitation (*pravāraṇā*).

While the *kaṭhina* ceremony for the invitation was being performed, many resident monks arrived; the visiting monks should have performed the invitation again, yet they did not do so according to the Dharma.

If the *pravāraṇā* has concluded, and the entire assembly has not yet risen, or if many have not yet risen, or if all have already risen, and many resident bhikṣus arrive, the visiting bhikṣus should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; otherwise, it is contrary to the Dharma.
At that time, there was a monastery where, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, resident monks arrived.
The resident monks knew that visiting monks had not yet arrived and thought:
"If we have five or more than five monks, we may perform the formal act (*karmavācanā*) of *pravāraṇā*."

“When the formal act (kamma) of the invitation ceremony (pravāraṇā) is being performed, if few guest bhikṣus arrive, the guest bhikṣus who are elders shall perform the invitation following the elder [of the resident community], and those who are juniors shall perform the invitation following the junior.”

If the *pravāraṇā* has concluded, whether the entire assembly has not yet risen, most have not yet risen, or all have already risen, and visiting bhikṣus arrive who are few in number, one should declare the purity of the *pravāraṇā*; if one does not so declare it, they must be dealt with according to the Dharma.
At that time, there was a residence where, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, an elder monk arrived.

"If we are five or more than five, we may perform the formal act (*karmavācanā*) of *pravāraṇā*."

If the *pravāraṇā* has concluded, whether the entire assembly has not yet risen, or many have not yet risen, or all have already risen, and many guest monks arrive, the resident monks should perform the *pravāraṇā* again; if they do not do so according to the Dharma, it is contrary to the rule."

Or it may be said:

"Destroy it! Thinking thus, he desires to employ various means to destroy the other, and then proceeds to perform the *karmavācanā* (formal act) of *pravāraṇā*.

At that time, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, if visiting bhikṣus arrive and see signs of resident bhikṣus—such as the arrangement of rope beds, wooden beds, bedding, woolen rugs, mattresses, pillows, and facilities for washing the feet—and seeing these signs, they do not seek them out but instead perform the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*.

If one performs the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*, the *karmavācanā pravāraṇā* is not accomplished and there is an offense.
Upon seeing signs [of his presence], one should seek him; if he cannot be found despite seeking, one should immediately summon him.

"Exterminate it!
Thinking thus, he employs various skillful means, desiring to cause the other to break [the harmony], and then performs the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*.

If one sees [a monk] and immediately seeks him out, but having sought him, does not find him, and having failed to find him, calls out to him and then performs the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*, that monk’s *karman* is not valid and he incurs no offense.

Upon seeing a sign, they immediately seek it; seeking it, they do not find it. Having failed to find it through their search, they then say: "It is lost!

If, by various skillful means, one intends to cause another to break [the harmony] and then performs the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*, that bhikṣu does not accomplish the *karman*, and [the instigator] incurs a *sthūlātyaya*.

If one obstructs a bhikṣu who is seeking to see [an offense] by requesting it, and though he requests it, he does not obtain it, and having failed to obtain it, he calls for a formal act (kamma) of self-indulgence (pārisuddhi), that bhikṣu’s formal act is not valid, yet he commits no offense.

If one sees [a fault] and immediately seeks it out, and having sought it, obtains it, and then performs the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*, that bhikṣu’s *karmavācanā* for *pravāraṇā* is valid, and he incurs no offense.

At that time, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, there were visiting bhikṣus at a certain residence who heard the voices of the resident bhikṣus—their sounds of walking up and down (*caṅkrama*), their coughing, their recitation of the sūtras, and their conversation—but hearing them, they did not seek them out, and they proceeded to perform the formal act (*karmavācanā*) of the *pravāraṇā*.
While the formal act (*kamma*) of the invitation (*pravāraṇā*) was being performed, an elder monk arrived.

"Seeking from what is heard," and so on, up to "the harmonious assembly for the *pravāraṇā*," is also like this.
"Hearing with doubt" is also like this.

At that time, there was a monastery where, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, an elder monk arrived. That monk’s formal act was not valid, and he was guilty of an offense.
"Seeking [the preceptor] based on what one has heard, and so forth, up to the harmonious assembly for the *pravāraṇā*, is also like this.

At that time, there was a residence where, on the day of the *pravāraṇā*, visiting bhikṣus arrived and saw resident bhikṣus on the boundary platform (*sīmāmaṇḍala*). If one sees [a monk] and seeks him out, and having sought him, invites him without calling him, yet proceeds with the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*, that bhikṣu’s *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā* is valid, and he incurs an offense.
If one sees him and seeks him out, and having sought him, calls him, and then performs the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*, that bhikṣu’s *karmavācanā* is not invalidated, and there is no offense.

At that time, the group of six bhikṣus thought to themselves:
"From a monastery where there are bhikṣus to a monastery where there are no bhikṣus, we fear that other bhikṣus will perform a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against us or obstruct our *pravāraṇā*."
The bhikṣus immediately informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"You should not harbor such a thought as this:

'From a monastery where there are bhikṣus, I shall go to a monastery where there are no bhikṣus, fearing that other bhikṣus might perform a formal act (karmavācanā) against me or obstruct my invitation to the end of the rains retreat (pravāraṇā).'"
That bhikṣu thought to himself:

The Buddha said:
"One should not entertain such a thought as this:

'From a place where there are bhikṣus and a residence, to a place where there are no bhikṣus and no residence, lest other bhikṣus perform a formal act (karmavācanā) against me or obstruct my invitation to the end of the retreat (pravāraṇā).'"

The Buddha said:
"You should not entertain such a thought as this:

'From a monastery where there are bhikṣus to a monastery where there are no bhikṣus, or to a place where there are no monasteries, or if I go to the boundary of the bhikṣu ordination platform, I fear that other bhikṣus will perform a *karmavācanā* against me or obstruct my *pravāraṇā*.'"
If one goes without the Saṃgha accompanying them and without any cause for departure, one incurs a *duṣkṛta* offense.

From a place where there are monks but no dwelling, to a place where there are neither monks nor a dwelling, it is also thus.
From a place where there are monks but no dwelling, to a place where there are neither monks nor a dwelling, yet there is a dwelling, it is also thus.
The same applies from the case where there are monks and there is a residence, or no residence, up to the case where there are no monks and there is a residence.
Likewise, it applies from the case where there are monks and there is a residence, or no residence, up to the case where there are no monks and there is no residence.
The same applies from the case where there are monks at a residence or no residence, up to the case where there are no monks at a residence or no residence.
It is likewise if it is for the sake of relatives, friends, or acquaintances.
At that time, the group of six bhikṣuṇīs formed this intention:

"We shall go inside the monastery and prevent the other bhikṣus from performing a formal act (*karmavācanā*) against the group of six bhikṣus, or from obstructing their invitation for the *pravāraṇā* ceremony."
The bhikṣus reported this to the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"A bhikṣuṇī should not entertain such an intention as:
'I shall go into the monastery and obstruct the other bhikṣus, saying:'"
"Do not perform a *kamma* against the group of six bhikṣus, nor obstruct their *pravāraṇā*.
One should not perform a *kamma* in the presence of bhikṣuṇīs, nor obstruct their *pravāraṇā*."

At that time, the bhikṣuṇīs sent śikṣamāṇās and śrāmaṇerikās into the monastery to block the other bhikṣus, so that they would not perform a *karmavācanā* against the group of six bhikṣus, nor obstruct their *pravāraṇā*.
The bhikṣus informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:

"A bhikṣuṇī should not send a śikṣamāṇā or a śrāmaṇerikā into the monastery to obstruct other bhikṣus, nor should she perform a formal act (karmavācanā) against the group of six bhikṣus, nor obstruct their invitation at the end of the rainy season retreat (pravāraṇā)."
"One should not perform a *karmavācanā* or obstruct the *pravāraṇā* ceremony in the presence of *śikṣamāṇās* or *śrāmaṇerīs.*" Those bhikṣuṇīs,
in turn, dispatched lay acquaintances to the monastery to obstruct the other bhikṣus, saying, "Do not perform a *karmavācanā* or obstruct the *pravāraṇā* for the group of six bhikṣus."
The bhikṣus informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"A bhikṣuṇī should not entertain such a thought as this:

'Send a lay acquaintance to go inside the monastery to obstruct other bhikṣus, so that they do not perform a formal act (karmavācanā) against the group of six bhikṣus, nor obstruct their invitation to the end of the rains retreat (pravāraṇā).'"
"One should not perform *karmavācanā* or suspend the *pravāraṇā* ceremony in the presence of laypeople.
At that time, King Prasenajit dispatched soldiers to guard the community of monks. The bhikṣus said to the soldiers, "Step aside;
we wish to perform the *karmavācanā* and the *pravāraṇā*."
The man replied, "The King has sent us to protect the community of monks; we do not dare go elsewhere now.
The bhikṣus informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"You should further tell them to move elsewhere. If they leave, that is well;

if they do not leave, you yourself should go to a place where they are neither seen nor heard and perform the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā*. You must not perform the *karmavācanā* for the *pravāraṇā* in the presence of those who have not yet received full ordination."
At that time, various devas, nāgas, and yakṣas came to listen to the *pravāraṇā*. A bhikṣu with the divine eye saw them, and having seen them, he felt a sense of awe and caution, thinking:
"The Buddha has not permitted us to perform the *pravāraṇā* in the presence of those who have not yet received the full ordination."
He immediately informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
"With the exception of those who have not yet received the full ordination (*upasampadā*), all others are permitted to perform the *pravāraṇā* before the formal ritual (*karmavācanā*).
Once they have completed the *pravāraṇā*, they sit for the recitation of the precepts (*poṣadha*) for so long that they become utterly exhausted."
The bhikṣus informed the Buddha, and the Buddha said:
“One should not recite the precepts again after the *pravāraṇā* has concluded; the *pravāraṇā* itself is the recitation of the precepts.
Thus spoke the Buddha.
The *Pravāraṇā-vastu* concludes. 2. The *Carman-vastu*. At that time, the Blessed One was staying in Rājagṛha.
At that time, there was a son of a great householder in the city of Campā named Śrona.
His parents had only this one son and cherished him dearly; having been accustomed to pleasure since birth, he had never walked upon the ground, and hair grew on the soles of his feet.

At that time, the King of Magadha heard that the son of a great elder in the city of Campā was dearly beloved by his parents; having been raised in luxury from birth, he had never walked upon the ground, and hair grew on the soles of his feet.
When he wished to see them later, he immediately commanded the lord of Campā:
"Let each of the elders bring his son to my presence.

Thereupon, the lord of Campā brought each of the sons to the presence of the King of Magadha. Having arrived, they prostrated themselves with their heads at the king's feet and stood to one side, addressing the king as follows:

“Your Majesty wishes to see the son of a great elder from the city of Campā. This boy has been accustomed to pleasure since birth; his parents dote on him and have never allowed him to walk upon the ground. Consequently, hair has grown on the soles of his feet. We pray that Your Majesty will permit us to spread a cloth upon the ground for him.”
The king said, "I grant permission for you to spread your robe upon the ground.
